rules.question: Does `added_code` `#[derive(Debug)]` on a struct or enum that has a field holding a secret — `password`, `secret`, `token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `api_key`, `private_key`, `client_secret`, session cookie, `Authorization` header value, card number — as a plain `String`, `Vec<u8>` or similar, so `{:?}`, `tracing` field capture or `unwrap` panic messages print it?
rules.true: A secret-bearing field is printed verbatim by the derived Debug implementation.
rules.false: Secret fields use a redacting wrapper (`secrecy::SecretString`/`SecretBox`, a newtype whose manual `Debug` prints `***`); the type implements `Debug` by hand and skips or redacts the field; or the field only names or points to a secret (`token_expires_at`, `api_key_id`, `secret_name`, `password_hash`).
rules.fix: Wrap the secret in secrecy::SecretString or a redacting newtype, or implement Debug by hand to redact it (OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet).

rules.question: Does `added_code` build a SQL statement with `format!`, `push_str`, `+` or `concat!` that interpolates a runtime value (a function parameter, request field, user input, id or search term) and pass it to a database call (`sqlx::query`/`query_as`/`query_scalar`, `execute`, `diesel::sql_query`, rusqlite `execute`/`prepare`/`query_row`, `tokio_postgres` `query`/`execute`), instead of using bind parameters?
rules.true: Runtime values are spliced into SQL text, opening SQL injection and breaking on quotes.
rules.false: Values are passed as bind parameters (`$1`/`?` with `.bind(v)`, `params![]`, `&[&v]`, `sqlx::query!`); the interpolated part is a compile-time constant or chosen from a fixed allowlist or enum of identifiers (table or column names, `ASC`/`DESC`); a query builder adds the values (`QueryBuilder::push_bind`, SeaQuery, Diesel DSL); or the string isn't SQL.
rules.fix: Pass values as bind parameters ($1 + .bind(v), params![]) instead of formatting them into the SQL string (OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet).

rules.question: Does `added_code` interpolate externally supplied text (a request field, command-line argument, environment value, filename, or function parameter) into a shell command string executed through std::process::Command or tokio::process::Command with sh/bash -c, cmd /C, or PowerShell -Command?
rules.true: Untrusted text becomes shell syntax instead of a literal argument, allowing command injection.
rules.false: The executable is invoked directly with separate arg/args values and no shell; the shell script is fixed and untrusted values are passed as positional arguments; values are selected from a fixed allowlist; a suitable shell-escaping API is used for the target shell; the command is only displayed; or no external value is interpolated into an executed shell command.
rules.fix: Invoke the executable directly with separate arguments, or keep the shell script fixed and pass data as positional arguments (Rust Command docs; OWASP OS Command Injection Defense).

rules.question: Does `added_code` extract a zip::ZipArchive entry by joining entry.name() or Path::new(entry.name()) directly to a destination and creating/writing that path, without enclosed_name or equivalent component validation that rejects absolute paths and parent-directory traversal?
rules.true: A ZIP entry controls the output path and can write outside the extraction directory via absolute paths or .. components.
rules.false: The entry path comes from enclosed_name and None is rejected, or equivalent validation rejects root/prefix and parent traversal; ZipArchive::extract handles paths; entry names are only listed or logged; extraction writes to an independently chosen fixed filename; or no ZIP entry is written to its archive-supplied path. This rule checks archive path validation, not preexisting filesystem symlinks.
rules.fix: Use ZipFile::enclosed_name() and reject invalid paths before joining the extraction root (zip ZipFile docs; CWE-22).

rules.question: Does `added_code` decide whether an untrusted filesystem path is confined to an allowed directory using string starts_with (including to_str/to_string_lossy/display().to_string()), so a sibling directory sharing the same textual prefix or unresolved .. components can pass the check before file access?
rules.true: A textual path-prefix authorization check can accept a path outside the allowed directory.
rules.false: The code canonicalizes paths and uses Path::starts_with for component-aware containment; it validates safe path components beneath a trusted root; it is checking URL prefixes or a filename naming convention rather than filesystem access authorization; a string check uses a separator boundary on already canonical paths; or no directory containment decision is made.
rules.fix: Resolve the candidate and root paths and compare them with component-aware Path::starts_with; avoid a string prefix as an authorization boundary (Rust Path docs; CWE-22).
